slides.sub: Bristol Sound. The night dance music became something you could not move to.

text: Jamaica's music came in through the port.
Out of that district, the music came.
slides.sub: The St. Pauls uprising. The ground the sound grew from.
1979 to 1988. The first definition of what Bristol sounded like.

text: Three of them left Wild Bunch.
slides.sub: Massive Attack. Later called the first trip-hop album. They never used that word.

slides.note: Unfinished Sympathy. 1991. BBC Radio 2: one of the most moving songs in dance music history. Nobody danced.

text: London put that label on us.
slides.sub: Portishead. Spy-film sound. Sadness made beautiful.
Wild Bunch scattered into three separate languages. All of them essential.

slides.strobe: The city that gave music weight asked nothing from your feet.
